concepts.title: The agent-governance budget decision
concepts.why_roles_may_frame_differently: The CISO may frame unauthorized access, inventory, containment, and assurance; the CFO may frame loss, investment gates, shared costs, insurance, and payback. This may be responsibility difference rather than disagreement.
concepts.missing_evidence: No verified finance role evidence, security role evidence, cost model, decision memo, or measured control outcome.
concepts.joint_discussion_could_clarify: Which event creates a dedicated budget, who owns it, what denominator supports the business case, and which outcomes justify renewal or shutdown.
concepts.format: Matched-deployment interview with one decision memo and one post-implementation review

sponsorship.conflict_risk: A vendor, insurer, or advisor could benefit from creating a new budget category.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Funding, product, insurance, advisory, and case relationships.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Sponsor has no participant, question, analysis, or approval role.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Rejected investments and null outcomes remain eligible.

concepts.title: Delegated authority versus task utility
concepts.why_roles_may_frame_differently: The CTO may optimize capability, latency, developer experience, and interoperability; the CISO may optimize least privilege, containment, monitoring, and auditability.
concepts.missing_evidence: No matched deployment compares task utility with attack, unauthorized-action, or operational burden outcomes.
concepts.joint_discussion_could_clarify: Where tighter authority actually reduces useful work, where scope correction removes apparent disagreement, and which risk tiers justify different controls.
concepts.format: Architecture review using the same deployment and four control patterns

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Protocol and platform interests may shape the framing.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No architecture secrets or participant data.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Tradeoffs and failed patterns must be publishable.

concepts.title: Speed, signature, and legal accountability
concepts.why_roles_may_frame_differently: The CEO may emphasize deployment pace, accountability, and competitive value; GC may emphasize authority allocation, evidence, privacy, contract, and regulatory exposure.
concepts.missing_evidence: No verified CEO or GC role-at-source-time corpus and no investigated case allocating responsibility among developer, deployer, user, platform, and tool provider.
concepts.joint_discussion_could_clarify: Which decisions are delegable, who signs, who remains accountable, and which evidence must exist before deployment.
concepts.format: Decision-rights scenario interview with jurisdiction-specific follow-up

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Legal or executive advisors may promote proprietary frameworks.

concepts.title: What the board can verify versus what the product team can measure
concepts.why_roles_may_frame_differently: The board may focus on materiality, assurance, risk appetite, and accountability; the product leader may focus on task success, iteration, architecture, and operational metrics.
concepts.missing_evidence: No verified board evidence, product-to-board metric lineage, or example where reporting changed a deployment decision.
concepts.joint_discussion_could_clarify: Which measures travel from runtime to board, who attests to them, and which metrics create false assurance.
concepts.format: Assurance-map interview tied to one board or risk-committee decision

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Assurance providers may favor more reporting or their own attestation model.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No board papers or respondent identities.

concepts.title: Control standardization versus local operating reality
concepts.why_roles_may_frame_differently: The operating partner may seek reusable controls, portfolio comparison, and investment visibility; the CIO may face legacy integration, local regulation, talent, reliability, and business-unit tradeoffs.
concepts.missing_evidence: No investor or operator evidence, portfolio denominator, negative cases, or cross-company implementation comparison.
concepts.joint_discussion_could_clarify: Which control fields can be standardized, which must remain local, and whether investor assurance changes actual outcomes.
concepts.format: Portfolio-pattern interview with anonymized company cases and no rankings

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Portfolio promotion, diligence signaling, and coercive participation.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Portfolio companies consent independently; no selection by sponsor.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No company-level results to funders or investors.

concepts.title: The agent-control thesis versus buyer evidence
concepts.why_roles_may_frame_differently: The investor may frame category formation, scale, and future value; the buyer may frame integration, control burden, procurement, failure, and measurable outcome.
concepts.missing_evidence: No verified investor thesis, buyer implementation, or linked claim-to-outcome comparison in the corpus.
concepts.joint_discussion_could_clarify: Which claims are investment hypotheses, which are buyer requirements, and what evidence would falsify either view.
concepts.format: Claim-evidence interview with an explicit no-pitch rule

sponsorship.required_disclosure: Holdings, advisory roles, and buyer-vendor relationships.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: No named portfolio preference or sales follow-up.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Public recording only; no attendee or buyer data.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Unfavorable and inconclusive evidence remains publishable.
